title: The Dancer Before the Idol
story:
BEFORE THE WORLD KNEW J-HOPE

Long before the world knew him as j-hope, Jung Hoseok had already built a reputation in the dance community of Gwangju.

As a member of the underground dance crew NEURON, he performed under the name **Smile Hoya**. He wasn't simply practicing dance in a studio anymore. He was taking part in the local street dance scene, performing, competing, and developing his own identity as a dancer.

THE ART OF MOVEMENT

Popping was one of his favorite styles, especially Boogaloo, a style known for its expressive body movements, isolations, and fluid way of dancing. He loved it so much that he sometimes practiced throughout the night. The dancers around him helped him develop his technique and explore different ways of moving to music.

RECOGNITION BEFORE DEBUT

And his dedication brought results. In a 2013 interview, j-hope looked back on his pre-debut years and recalled receiving numerous awards for dancing in Gwangju. He also mentioned winning an underground dance battle and performing at a festival.

His reputation was not limited to his own memories. In the same interview, V recalled that people at his school already knew j-hope as the talented dancer from a dance academy in Gwangju. Even before BTS debuted, his dancing had made an impression on people around him.

These experiences gave him something that went far beyond technical skills. He had learned how to perform, how to compete, how to express himself through movement, and how to command attention on stage.

FROM DANCER TO IDOL

When he eventually joined Big Hit, he brought all of that experience with him. He was entering a new world as a trainee, but dance was already the field in which he had years of experience and confidence.

He wasn't an idol who became a dancer. He was a dancer who became an idol.

Before the world knew j-hope, the dance community already knew **Smile Hoya**.
